name: Acromegaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for Acromegaly

criteria.description: Elevated serum insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) above age- and sex-adjusted normal range
Failure of GH suppression to <1 ng/mL (or <0.4 ng/mL with sensitive assay) during 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT)
Characteristic clinical features (acral enlargement, coarsened facial features, soft tissue swelling)
Random GH >1 ng/mL (screening, not diagnostic alone)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated IGF-1 plus failure of GH suppression on OGTT. If IGF-1 elevated and clinical features obvious, OGTT may be omitted in some guidelines.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Average diagnostic delay is 7-10 years from symptom onset. Over 95% of cases are caused by a GH-secreting pituitary adenoma (somatotropinoma).

pathognomonic.notes: Increased ring size, shoe size over time; patients may not notice gradual change

pathognomonic.symptomName: Coarsened facial features (frontal bossing, prognathism, enlarged nose and lips)

common.notes: Due to macroglossia and soft tissue hypertrophy of upper airway

occasional.notes: Due to optic chiasm compression by macroadenoma
Due to GH/prolactin co-secretion or stalk effect

rare.notes: Due to cavernous sinus invasion by large adenomas

laboratory: Elevated serum IGF-1 above age-/sex-matched normal range
Failure of GH suppression to <1 ng/mL on 75g OGTT
Random GH levels >1 ng/mL (pulsatile secretion complicates interpretation)
imaging: Pituitary MRI with gadolinium showing adenoma (macroadenoma in ~70%)
Skull X-ray showing enlarged sella turcica, thickened calvarium (historical)
Hand X-ray showing tufting of distal phalanges, widened joint spaces
Sleep study (polysomnography) for obstructive sleep apnea
genetic: AIP mutations in familial isolated pituitary adenoma (FIPA), especially in younger patients
McCune-Albright syndrome (GNAS1 mutations) in rare cases
other: Visual field testing (Goldmann or Humphrey perimetry)
Colonoscopy screening for colorectal polyps at diagnosis
Assessment of pituitary function (other axes: thyroid, adrenal, gonadal)

distinguishingFeatures: Gigantism causes excessive linear growth rather than acral changes
Same pathophysiology but different presentation due to open growth plates
Pachydermoperiostosis has normal IGF-1 and GH
Hypothyroidism has coarse features but no true acral enlargement
TSH elevated, free T4 low in hypothyroidism
Myxedema rather than soft tissue hypertrophy
Paget's shows characteristic bone scan findings
Paget's involves specific bones rather than diffuse enlargement

redFlags: Visual field loss suggesting chiasmal compression (needs urgent surgical evaluation)
Pituitary apoplexy (acute headache, vision loss, meningismus)
Onset in children/adolescents (consider gigantism; evaluate for AIP/MEN1/X-LAG mutations)
Rapid symptom progression suggesting aggressive or malignant pituitary tumor
references: Katznelson L, et al. Acromegaly: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2014;99(11):3933-51.
Melmed S. Acromegaly pathogenesis and treatment. J Clin Invest. 2009;119(11):3189-202.
Colao A, et al. Acromegaly. Lancet. 2019;394(10207):1341-1353.
Fleseriu M, et al. Acromegaly: pathogenesis, diagnosis, and management. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2022;10(11):804-826.
